title: greeter.toml should be in backup=()
body:
cachyos-hypr-noctalia 1.2.4-2 ships /var/lib/noctalia-greeter/greeter.toml as a plain tracked file, but it's a user-editable config the greeter also rewrites at runtime. So upgrades hard-fail with a file conflict for anyone who already has one, and otherwise silently overwrite the user's settings.

console
$ pacman -Qo /var/lib/noctalia-greeter/greeter.toml
... owned by cachyos-hypr-noctalia 1.2.4-2
$ pacman -Qii cachyos-hypr-noctalia | grep greeter.toml   # (empty — not a backup file)

Fix: add var/lib/noctalia-greeter/greeter.toml to backup=() so pacman preserves it and uses .pacnew.

title: Fix workspace keybinds for AZERTY layout using keycodes
body:
On AZERTY keyboards the number-row keys emit symbols (& é " ' ...) rather than digits without Shift, so binding workspace switching to the digit characters does not work. Bind by physical evdev keycode instead (1..9 => code:10..18, 0 => code:19) via a small digitCode() helper.

Applies to workspace focus (absolute + relative) and move-window-to- workspace bindings.

This fix should correspond to AZERTY and QWERTY keyboards without requiring any modification

title: Hyprland: nwg-displays saves to ~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua but the skeleton never loads it (require("monitors") missing from hyprland.lua)
body:
## Environment

- CachyOS, cachyos-hypr-noctalia 1.2.5-1 (Hyprland skeleton from /etc/skel)
- hyprland 0.56.2-2.1 (CachyOS build, Lua config)
- nwg-displays 0.4.4-1 (vanilla Arch `extra` package, no distro patches)

## Summary

CachyOS's Hyprland skeleton (`/etc/skel/.config/hypr/`) uses the Lua config
system (Hyprland ≥ 0.55), with `hyprland.lua` containing
`require("config.monitors")` etc. The nwg-displays GUI, when configured for
Hyprland ≥ 0.55, saves monitor settings to `~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua`
(root level) and the upstream README instructs users to load that file by
adding `require("monitors")` to their config.

The CachyOS skeleton does not include that `require("monitors")` line. As a
result, everything nwg-displays saves is written to a file that nothing ever
loads: the GUI reports success, `hyprctl reload` runs, and the display layout
never changes — not even after reboot. Users end up hand-editing
`~/.config/hypr/config/monitors.lua` or asking on forums, defeating the
purpose of the GUI.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Fresh CachyOS install with the Hyprland (Noctalia) edition.
2. Run `nwg-displays`, arrange monitors (e.g. move external display), Apply.
   - nwg-displays writes `hl.monitor({...})` blocks to
     `~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua` and runs `hyprctl reload` (its intended
     flow per README).
3. Nothing changes. Re-login / reboot — still nothing changes.
4. `cat ~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua` shows the saved, valid config that is
   simply never loaded.

## Evidence that the file is orphaned

The session journal proves the Lua entry point and which files it pulls in:

    [cfg] Regular config at ~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua
    [cfg] Using lua config found at ~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua

and the skeleton `hyprland.lua` (identical to current master
`etc/skel/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua`) requires only:

    require("config.animations") ... require("config.monitors") ... etc.

There is no `require("monitors")` and no other path that would load a
root-level `monitors.lua`.

Cross-check that the legacy `hyprland.conf` route is indeed not involved:

    $ hyprctl getoption animations:enabled
    bool: true
    set: false        # (a stale hyprland.conf set it to false — it is not loaded)

nwg-displays side (vanilla 0.4.4, `settings_applier.py`):

    save_list_to_text_file(lines_lua, outputs_path_lua)   # ~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua
    hyprctl("reload")

This matches the upstream README instruction: *"For version 0.55 and greater
(using Lua), insert this line: require("monitors")"* — the step that the
CachyOS skeleton is missing.

## Impact

- Every user of the CachyOS Hyprland edition who tries to configure displays
  via nwg-displays gets a silent no-op (including workspace→monitor
  assignments via the parallel `workspaces.lua` path).
- The failure mode is misleading: save succeeds, reload runs, a confirmation
  dialog appears — there is no error anywhere to explain why nothing applies.

## Suggested fix (one-liner)

Add the nwg-displays integration lines to the skeleton, e.g.:

```lua
-- nwg-displays integration (writes ~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua / workspaces.lua)
require("monitors")
require("workspaces")
```

(or comment them in `hyprland.lua` with a note so users who enable
nwg-displays can uncomment them).

Alternative: ship a compatibility symlink in the skeleton
(`~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua -> config/monitors.lua`), which also works —
verified locally — but the explicit `require` matches upstream nwg-displays
documentation and is less surprising.

## Verified workaround currently in use

    ln -sfn config/monitors.lua ~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua
    ln -sfn config/workspaces.lua ~/.config/hypr/workspaces.lua

After symlinking, nwg-displays Apply writes through to the loaded file and
changes apply live (verified by write-through test and live `hyprctl monitors
-j` checks).

## Side note

On this Lua-config build, `hyprctl keyword` is fully blocked ("keyword can't work
with non-legacy parsers. Use eval."), and `hyprctl eval 'monitor=...'` fails as
Lua syntax — but a working runtime bypass exists and was verified:

```bash
# monitor geometry (live, equivalent to legacy keyword)
hyprctl eval 'hl.monitor({output="DP-12", mode="1920x1080@120", position="0x0", scale=1.0})'
# any config option
hyprctl eval 'hl.config({cursor={zoom_factor=2.0}})'
# multiple statements: IIFE
hyprctl eval '(function() hl.config({cursor={zoom_factor=2.0}}); hl.config({general={gaps_in=5}}) end)()'
```

Semantics match the legacy `keyword` (runtime override, reset by `hyprctl reload`).
Caveat: `eval` silently returns "ok" for Lua-valid but inert code (e.g.
`monitor=eDP-1` is just a global assignment), so only `hl.*` API calls actually
apply. A `keyword`-compatible shim or documentation of this pattern would help
scripts migrating to the Lua parser.

title: hyprctl keyword blocked on Lua parser (exit 0 on error) and eval silently returns "ok" for inert code — only hl.* API calls apply
body:
## Environment

- CachyOS, hyprland 0.56.2-2.1 (Lua config system, Hyprland ≥ 0.55)
- cachyos-hypr-noctalia 1.2.5-1 (Hyprland skeleton)
- Wayland session, Hyprland 0.56.2

## Summary

On the Lua config build, `hyprctl keyword` is rejected for **everything** —
including legacy keywords — and the error message says "Use eval.". But
`eval` executes **Lua code**, not config syntax, so the obvious migration
path dead-ends in one of two hostile ways:

1. config syntax → hard Lua syntax error, or
2. Lua-valid but inert code → **silent "ok" with no effect**.

The only working runtime path (calling the `hl.*` Lua API through `eval`) is
undiscoverable from the error message or help text. Net effect: every script
or keybind workflow that used `hyprctl keyword` for runtime tweaks breaks on
this build, and the suggested replacement either crashes or silently no-ops.

## Repro (all outputs verbatim from the affected machine)

```bash
# 1) keyword is rejected for everything — even legacy keywords — and exits 0 on failure
$ hyprctl keyword cursor:zoom_factor 1.5
keyword can't work with non-legacy parsers. Use eval.        # exit code: 0

$ hyprctl keyword workspace "5,monitor:DP-12"
keyword can't work with non-legacy parsers. Use eval.        # exit code: 0

# 2) The suggested "eval" path fails on config syntax:
$ hyprctl eval 'monitor=eDP-1,2880x1800@120,1920x0,1.5'
error: [string "monitor=eDP-1,2880x1800@120,1920x0,1.5"]:1: malformed number near '2880x'

# 3) …or worse, silently "succeeds" while doing nothing:
$ hyprctl eval 'monitor=eDP'
ok        # ← just a global Lua variable assignment; monitors unchanged, no warning

# 4) print() output is swallowed, so eval can't be used to read state back either
$ hyprctl eval 'print("hello from hyprland lua")'
ok
```

Note the contrast: a bad *API call* errors properly
(`hl.not_an_api()` → `attempt to call a nil value`), while inert-but-valid
Lua returns "ok" — so scripts cannot distinguish "applied" from "no-op"
without a follow-up read via `hyprctl getoption` / `monitors -j`.

## The working (but undocumented) bypass — verified

```bash
# monitor geometry — actually applies (verified via `hyprctl monitors -j`)
hyprctl eval 'hl.monitor({output="DP-12", mode="1920x1080@120", position="0x0", scale=1.0})'

# config options — applies and is visible to `hyprctl getoption` (set: true)
hyprctl eval 'hl.config({cursor={zoom_factor=2.0}})'

# multiple statements — wrap in an IIFE
hyprctl eval '(function() hl.config({cursor={zoom_factor=2.0}}); hl.config({general={gaps_in=5}}) end)()'
```

Semantics match the legacy `keyword`: runtime override, reset by
`hyprctl reload` (verified: zoom_factor 2.5 → reload → back to config
default 1.0, monitor layout preserved). The gap is purely discoverability
and scripting ergonomics.

## Impact

- Runtime-tweak scripts (monitor presets, profile switchers, keybind-launched
  layout changes) built on `hyprctl keyword` fail on this build.
- Scripting-hostile failure modes: exit code **0** on the keyword error, and
  "ok" for inert eval code.

## Suggested improvements (any of)

1. Restore a `keyword`-compatible path on the Lua parser — internally
   translate `name=value` / `name value` into the corresponding
   `hl.config` / monitor API call.
2. Or: make the error message teach the working pattern, e.g.
   `Use eval, e.g.: hyprctl eval 'hl.monitor({output="DP-1", mode="...", position="...", scale=1})'`
3. Make `eval` warn (or fail) when the snippet performs no `hl.*` side
   effects, and return non-zero exit codes on errors.
4. Document the `hl.*` runtime API (monitor/config/dispatch/…) reachable
   via `hyprctl eval` in the wiki / `hyprctl --help`.

## Venue note

This is core `hyprctl` behavior of the Lua config system, so it may belong
upstream at hyprwm/Hyprland — happy to cross-post there if that's the right
home. Filed here because it directly affects the CachyOS-shipped build and
the runtime workflows around the CachyOS Hyprland skeleton. (Related:
#39 — nwg-displays saves that the skeleton never loads.)

title: fix(repo): remove Bibata-Modern-Ice cursor from tree
Run noctalia as a systemd user service so a killed shell comes back
body:
## Problem

`config/autostart.lua` starts the shell with a one-shot exec:

```lua
hl.exec_cmd("noctalia")
```

Nothing supervises that process. Anything that kills it — a crash, or an OOM kill under memory
pressure, which is exactly what `earlyoom` does on a loaded machine — leaves the session with a
compositor, working windows, and **no bar, no launcher, no notifications**.

The symptom misleads. Super+Space does nothing, so it reads as a broken keybind or a broken
launcher, and the obvious reaction is to restart Hyprland — which closes every window and fixes
nothing. The shell is simply gone:

```
$ hyprctl clients | jq length      # windows are fine
$ hyprctl layers                   # no noctalia layer surfaces at all
$ pgrep -x noctalia                # empty
```

I hit this on CachyOS after an `earlyoom` kill: `hyprctl layers` had no `noctalia-bar-default`,
and the Super+Space bind resolved to `noctalia msg panel-toggle launcher`, an IPC call into a
process that did not exist. Starting the shell by hand fixed it, and it was killed again minutes
later by an OOM pass — with nothing to restart it.

## Change

A systemd user unit owns the process, so `Restart=always` brings the shell back:

* **new** `etc/skel/.config/systemd/user/noctalia.service` — `Type=simple`, `Restart=always`,
  `PartOf=`/`After=`/`WantedBy=graphical-session.target`
* `config/autostart.lua` — `hl.exec_cmd("systemctl --user start noctalia.service")`. Starting an
  already-active unit is a no-op, so a session gets exactly one instance whether or not the unit
  has been enabled, and `systemctl --user daemon-reload` is not needed at login.
* `README.md` — one short subsection, including "if Super+Space stops working, check
  `systemctl --user status noctalia` before restarting anything".

## Verification

On Hyprland 0.57.0 / uwsm / noctalia 5.4.1, with the equivalent unit installed locally:

```
$ systemctl --user kill --signal=TERM noctalia.service
$ sleep 12
$ systemctl --user is-active noctalia.service
active                      # MainPID 787990 -> 788440
$ hyprctl layers | grep noctalia
noctalia-bar-default  noctalia-wallpaper
$ noctalia msg panel-toggle launcher
ok
```

The `uwsm` user manager already carries `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`/`DISPLAY` in its environment, so the
unit starts against the live session without extra `PassEnvironment`/`Environment=` lines.

## Notes

* This deliberately does not touch the compositor or the keybinds — the shell is the layer that
  failed, and it is the layer that should restart.
* Users who prefer to keep the old behaviour can delete the unit and restore
  `hl.exec_cmd("noctalia")`; nothing else depends on it.
* I did not add `MemoryMax=`/`OOMPolicy=` here: a memory ceiling is a user's tuning decision, not
  a sensible distro default. (Locally I do run one, which is how the unit behaves under pressure.)

title: Hyprland ignores the keyboard layout chosen in the installer (always starts with `us`)
body:
### Description

When CachyOS is installed with the Hyprland desktop, the keyboard layout selected in the installer is not applied to the Hyprland session: it always starts with the `us` layout. The TTY console uses the selected layout correctly.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Boot the official CachyOS ISO and start Calamares.
2. Select a non-US keyboard layout (e.g. `es`).
3. Select **Hyprland** as the desktop and finish the installation.
4. Log in to the Hyprland session and type.

**Expected:** the selected layout (`es`).
**Actual:** `us`.

Reproduced on a fresh installation from the official ISO currently offered for download (`260809`).

### Cause

Hyprland only takes the layout from its own config (`input.kb_layout`). It does not read any of the system-wide files where the installers store the selection:

- Calamares (`keyboard` module, `SetKeyboardLayoutJob.cpp`, branch `cachyos-staging` @ `42a91ab23`) writes `/etc/vconsole.conf` (`KEYMAP`, `XKBLAYOUT`, `XKBMODEL`, …), `/etc/X11/xorg.conf.d/00-keyboard.conf` and `/etc/default/keyboard`.
- The CLI installer (New-Cli-Installer) writes `KEYMAP=` to `/etc/vconsole.conf` and `XkbLayout` to `/etc/X11/xorg.conf.d/00-keyboard.conf`.

`etc/skel/.config/hypr/config/inputs.lua` (current `master`, `467067b5a`) does not set `kb_layout`, so Hyprland falls back to its default `us`.

### Suggested fix

Have the dotfiles read the system X11 keymap when Hyprland starts, instead of each installer having to edit the user's config. `/etc/X11/xorg.conf.d/00-keyboard.conf` is a good source because:

- both installers write it (`/etc/vconsole.conf` only has `XKBLAYOUT` with Calamares, not with the CLI installer);
- it is the file `systemd-localed` maintains, so `localectl set-x11-keymap` would also be honoured.

Something along these lines in `config/inputs.lua` (untested sketch):

```lua
-- Use the system keyboard layout (written by the installer / localectl)
local function system_xkb()
    local xkb = {}
    local f = io.open("/etc/X11/xorg.conf.d/00-keyboard.conf", "r")
    if not f then return xkb end
    for line in f:lines() do
        local key, value = line:match('^%s*Option%s+"(Xkb%a+)"%s+"([^"]*)"')
        if key and value ~= "" then xkb[key] = value end
    end
    f:close()
    return xkb
end

local xkb = system_xkb()

hl.config({
    input = {
        kb_layout  = xkb.XkbLayout or "us",
        kb_variant = xkb.XkbVariant or "",
        kb_model   = xkb.XkbModel or "",
        -- sensitivity = -0.25,
        accel_profile = "flat",
    },
})
```

If the file is missing, the behaviour stays as it is now (`us`). Omarchy solves the same problem in a similar way (it reads `XKBLAYOUT`/`XKBVARIANT` from `/etc/vconsole.conf` in `default/hypr/keyboard.lua`).

One caveat for non-Latin layouts (e.g. `ru`): Hyprland resolves keybindings against the first layout in `kb_layout`, so `SUPER` + letter bindings stop working unless a Latin layout comes first (e.g. `us,ru`).

I'm happy to send a PR if this approach sounds good.
